title: Safe Batch Rename
statement:
Write `rename_ext.sh DIR FROM TO` that renames files in `DIR` (not recursively) whose names end in `.FROM` so they end in `.TO` instead, e.g. `rename_ext.sh photos jpeg jpg`.

- For each rename, print `renamed: OLD -> NEW` (just the file names) to stdout, in sorted order.
- **Never overwrite:** if the new name already exists, leave both files alone, print `skip: OLD` to stderr, and exit 1 at the end.
- Only regular files are renamed (not directories), and only an exact `.FROM` suffix counts (`a.jpeg.bak` doesn't).
- Names may contain spaces or start with `-`.
- If nothing matches, print nothing and exit 0.
- Wrong number of arguments: usage on stderr, exit 2.
starter_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# rename_ext.sh DIR FROM TO
cd $1
for f in *.$2; do
  mv $f ${f%.$2}.$3
done
harness:
(
  cd "$(fresh_dir)"; mkdir p; touch p/a.jpeg p/b.jpeg p/keep.png
  run_solution p jpeg jpg
  if [[ $status == 0 && $out == $'renamed: a.jpeg -> a.jpg\nrenamed: b.jpeg -> b.jpg' && -f p/a.jpg && -f p/b.jpg && ! -e p/a.jpeg && -f p/keep.png ]]; then
    pass "renames matching files and reports each"
  else fail "renames matching files and reports each" "status=$status stdout=[$out] files=[$(ls p | tr '\n' ' ')]"; fi
)
(
  cd "$(fresh_dir)"; mkdir p; touch "p/summer trip.jpeg" "p/-dash.jpeg"
  run_solution p jpeg jpg
  if [[ -f "p/summer trip.jpg" && -f p/-dash.jpg && $status == 0 ]]; then pass "spaces and leading dashes"
  else fail "spaces and leading dashes" "status=$status stderr=[$err] files=[$(ls p | tr '\n' '|')]"; fi
)
(
  cd "$(fresh_dir)"; mkdir p; touch p/x.png
  run_solution p jpeg jpg
  if [[ $status == 0 && -z $out && -z $err && -f p/x.png ]]; then pass "no matches: no output, exit 0"
  else fail "no matches: no output, exit 0" "status=$status stdout=[$out] stderr=[$err] files=[$(ls p | tr '\n' ' ')]"; fi
)
(
  cd "$(fresh_dir)"; mkdir p
  echo old > p/a.jpg; echo new > p/a.jpeg; touch p/b.jpeg
  run_solution p jpeg jpg
  if [[ $status == 1 && $err == *"skip: a.jpeg"* && $(cat p/a.jpg) == old && $(cat p/a.jpeg) == new && -f p/b.jpg ]]; then
    pass "never overwrites: skip, keep going, exit 1"
  else fail "never overwrites: skip, keep going, exit 1" "status=$status stderr=[$err] a.jpg=[$(cat p/a.jpg 2>&1)]"; fi
)
(
  cd "$(fresh_dir)"; mkdir -p p/album.jpeg; touch p/a.jpeg.bak p/notjpeg
  run_solution p jpeg jpg
  if [[ -d p/album.jpeg && -f p/a.jpeg.bak && -f p/notjpeg && -z $out ]]; then pass "only regular files with the exact suffix"
  else fail "only regular files with the exact suffix" "stdout=[$out] files=[$(ls p | tr '\n' ' ')]"; fi
)
(
  cd "$(fresh_dir)"; mkdir p
  run_solution p jpeg
  if [[ $status == 2 && $err == *usage* ]]; then pass "wrong argument count: usage, exit 2"
  else fail "wrong argument count: usage, exit 2" "status=$status stderr=[$err]"; fi
)
reference_solution:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# rename_ext.sh DIR FROM TO
if (( $# != 3 )); then
  echo "usage: rename_ext.sh DIR FROM TO" >&2
  exit 2
fi
dir=$1 from=$2 to=$3

shopt -s nullglob   # a pattern that matches nothing expands to nothing (not to itself)
status=0
for path in "$dir"/*."$from"; do   # quoted parts are literal; only * is a glob
  [[ -f $path ]] || continue       # skip directories (and anything else)
  new=${path%."$from"}.$to
  if [[ -e $new ]]; then
    echo "skip: ${path##*/}" >&2
    status=1
    continue
  fi
  mv -- "$path" "$new"             # -- : a name like "-dash.jpeg" is not an option
  echo "renamed: ${path##*/} -> ${new##*/}"
done
exit "$status"
hints: Without `shopt -s nullglob`, a pattern that matches nothing stays as the literal text `*.jpeg`, and your loop runs once with that.
Glob directly with quotes around the variable parts: `for path in "$dir"/*."$from"`. Never parse `ls`.
Check `[[ -e $new ]]` before moving. `mv -n` exists, but it doesn't tell you it skipped anything.
`mv -- "$path" "$new"`: `--` ends option parsing, so `-dash.jpeg` isn't read as an option.
discussion:
Batch renames are where scripts destroy data, so the goal is **safe by default**:

- **Never clobber.** `mv a.jpeg a.jpg` silently replaces an existing `a.jpg`. Check first, report, and make the exit status reflect partial failure.
- **The unmatched-glob trap.** By default, `*.jpeg` with no matches expands to the literal string `*.jpeg`. Your loop then tries to rename a file called `*.jpeg`, an error at best. `shopt -s nullglob` (or a `[[ -e ]]` guard) fixes it.
- **`--` before file names**, because names can start with `-`. `mv -dash.jpeg x` would be read as options.
- **Don't `cd` blindly.** `cd $1` with an unquoted, unchecked argument means a typo runs the loop in the wrong directory. Glob relative to `"$dir"` instead.
- Glob results come out sorted (in the C locale), which is why the output order is predictable.

A good habit for real batch operations: add a `-n` (dry-run) flag that prints what *would* happen. People trust tools they can preview.

**Follow-ups:** How would you make this recursive safely? What does `set -euo pipefail` do, and where does it surprise people?
